subject: Clarify: penetration test coverage & responsibilities across hosting variants
messages:
From: BluePeak Security <engagement@bluepeaksec.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: NimbusRetail Security <security@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 08:53:00 -0800
Subject: Questions: penetration test coverage across hosting models

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for agreeing to work with BluePeak for the upcoming penetration test for NimbusRetail. Before we finalize the Statement of Work, we need a clear understanding of what parts of Redwood’s platform are considered in-scope for a customer-requested external pen test for the different hosting options (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private/VPC, on-prem). Specifically: 

- Which network endpoints or public IP ranges will we be testing for each hosting variant?
- For Dedicated and Private deployments, what parts are the customer responsibility vs Redwood responsibility?
- Are model weights, KV cache stores, and managed control plane APIs in scope for Hosted and Dedicated tests?

Could you also share the asset/inventory and architecture artifacts you typically provide to external testers, and any temporary test accounts or allowlists you require?

Attached: sample_test_matrix_questions.pdf (attachment stub)

Appreciate a short matrix so we can lock in test windows.

—Sam Lal
Engagement Lead, BluePeak Security
engagement@bluepeaksec.com

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: BluePeak Security <engagement@bluepeaksec.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, NimbusRetail Security <security@nimbusretail.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Nov 2028 11:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Questions: penetration test coverage across hosting models

Sam — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR: scope differs by hosting variant; control plane and multi-tenant shared services are handled differently. See details below and I’ll attach our one-page coverage matrix.

Hosted API (Redwood-hosted):
- In-scope for customer-authorized external tests: public API endpoints for the customer’s org key, the edge/API gateway IPs, and any platform-managed integrations exposed to the internet.
- Out-of-scope: Redwood-managed multi-tenant control plane internals (internal admin consoles, orchestration control plane), and third-party cloud provider management planes.
- Artifacts we provide: hosting_scope_matrix.xlsx, public endpoint list, temporary test API keys (scoped & rate-limited).

Dedicated (reserved capacity):
- In-scope: the dedicated GPU instances, load balancers assigned to the customer, and the control-plane interfaces that are dedicated to the customer (if configured).
- Shared/Out-of-scope: hardware-level host OS images managed by the cloud provider and Redwood’s global shared telemetry backplane.
- Artifacts: dedicated-deployment-arch.png, dedicated-instance-list.csv, network ACL summary.

Private / VPC (customer-managed networking):
- Typically in-scope only for the customer’s VPC endpoints and resources; Redwood’s control plane operates via a private connector and we treat the customer VPC boundary as the primary responsibility of the customer. We will provide integration points and a list of expected ingress/egress flows.

On-prem:
- Out-of-scope unless we have a dedicated on-prem engagement (separate SOW).

Regarding model weights and KV cache: for Hosted, model weights are stored in Redwood-managed storage and are considered part of Redwood’s managed infrastructure (we will assess and provide SOC2 artifacts). For Dedicated, if weights are hosted within the customer-dedicated instances we will include them in scope per the SOW.

Next steps: I’ll upload the hosting scope matrix and the SOW to DocuSign and share links. Please confirm target test dates and whether you need remediation contacts and escalation SLAs in advance.

Attachments: redwood_hosting_scope_matrix.xlsx (will attach after internal review)

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Trust & Safety, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Questions: penetration test coverage across hosting models

Adding engineering detail so testers know what we can (and cannot) expose: 

1) Asset inventory we will deliver: list of IPs/hostnames, service ports, load balancer IDs, and logical service ownership.
2) Credentials & access: short-lived test API keys (scoped to dev/test environments) and a jumpbox VPN account for access to dedicated environments if required.
3) Model artifacts: for Hosted, we cannot ship model weights; we will provide a description of storage controls and access logs. For Dedicated, weights are accessible on the dedicated instance; tests that require access to underlying filesystem must be explicitly in the SOW.
4) KV cache & ephemeral token stores: these are considered application-layer caches. For Hosted customers we consider them managed; we can provide test endpoints that exercise cache behavior without exposing underlying storage. For Dedicated we can provide either blackbox access or, if requested and SOW-approved, whitebox access under supervision.

Out-of-scope clarifications: third-party cloud provider infra (hypervisor/host firmware), customer-managed VPC-internal services (these remain customer responsibility), and any upstream SaaS integrations (e.g., logging SaaS) unless a separate authorization is granted.

We’ll prepare: redwood_hosting_scope_matrix.xlsx (v2), dedicated-instance-list.csv, and a short remediation SLAs doc. ETA for docs: EOD tomorrow (11/17).

—Karthik

2) We need the signed SOW and the DocuSign access window; please confirm the date range you want testing to occur and the point people for remediation (we’ll need 24/7 contact during the test window).

Sam / BluePeak,

Appended the deliverables and a one-page decision matrix to this thread. Quick answers and actions: 

- Model weights and persisted KV cache:
  - Hosted: Treated as Redwood-managed; blackbox active testing that targets public endpoints is permitted, but any tests that attempt to enumerate or access underlying storage endpoints must be authorized and will be executed in a controlled whitebox mode with Redwood engineering present.
  - Dedicated: In-scope if the customer SOW specifies whitebox access — we can enable supervised filesystem access on dedicated instances per request.

- SOW & dates: I’ve uploaded the signed SOW to DocuSign (link below). Proposed test window: 2028-12-04 to 2028-12-08. Confirm ASAP if that works for NimbusRetail.

- Remediation / escalation contacts:
